title: Grade 10 Biology National Exam & Practice 2017 (5 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 5 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: The finding of the study conducted in two different villages showed that there are harmful practices that affect reproductive health. The common practices in village 1 were forcing underage girls to get married based norms, and sexual abuse or harassment. In village 2 abduction to make the girl a wife unwillingly was very rampant. Which one of the following options is correct about the two villages?
options: In village 1, gender-based violence,kidnapping and female genital mutilation are common.
In village 1, gender-based violence and early marriage are common.
In village 2, kidnapping and female genital mutilation are common.
In village 2, gender-based violence and female genital mutilation are common.
questions.explanation:
In village 1, the harmful practices include forcing underage girls into marriage (early marriage) and sexual abuse or harassment (gender-based violence).

 Village 2 is characterized mainly by abduction for forced marriage, not the practices listed in the other options.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about mitosis? It is a division of
options: somatic cells to make daughter cells with half chromosome.
sex cells to make identical daughter cells with doubled chromosome.
somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
sex cells to make different daughter cells.
questions.explanation:
Mitosis is the process by which somatic (body) cells divide to produce two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

 It is not involved in producing sex cells (gametes), which occurs via meiosis.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following features is common for mitosis and meiosis? They both involve
options: replication of DNA and the formation of daughter cells.
production of daughter cells identical to the parent cell.
formation of cells with the same chromosome number as parent cell.
spermatogenesis and oogenesis processes in males and females.
questions.explanation:
Both mitosis and meiosis begin with the replication of DNA during the S phase of interphase. After this, both processes involve the division of the cell to form daughter cells.

 However, mitosis produces genetically identical cells, while meiosis produces genetically varied gametes with half the chromosome number.

questions.questionText: What does it mean if an animal is poikilothermic? It
options: changes its body temperature with environmental condition.
increases its metabolic rate during cold and hot conditions.
keeps its body temperature constant regardless of external changes.
produces heat when temperature falls by activating the hypothalamus.
questions.explanation: A poikilothermic animal, also called cold-blooded, cannot internally regulate its body temperature. Its body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment, unlike homeothermic animals which maintain a constant internal temperature.

questions.questionText: If progesterone remains high after ovulation, what will be the most likely outcome?
options: FSH will be produced rapidly which leads to a new cycle.
Oestrogen will be decreased, closing down the lining of the uterus.
Uterus lining will be maintained and prepared for pregnancy.
Corpus luteum will be regenerated, inhibiting hormone production.
questions.explanation:
High levels of progesterone after ovulation maintain the endometrium (uterine lining), making it suitable for implantation of a fertilized egg.

 If pregnancy does not occur, progesterone levels drop, leading to menstruation.

questions.questionText: The most reliable contraceptive method that prevents travelling of ovum from the ovaries through the fallopian tubes, but requires surgery is
questions.explanation:
Sterilization (like tubal ligation in females) is a surgical method that blocks or cuts the fallopian tubes, preventing the ovum from traveling from the ovaries to the uterus.

 It is considered highly reliable and permanent. Other methods like IUDs, spermicides, or injections do not block the ovum physically through the tubes.

questions.questionText: Among the following, which one increases the risk to be infected by sexually transmitted infections?
options: Have no history of sexually transmitted infections
Misuse of drugs that inhibit your judgment
Protective sexual contact and medical treatment
Consistent use of condoms during intercourse
questions.explanation:
The misuse of drugs can impair judgment and lead to risky sexual behaviors, such as unprotected sex or multiple partners, which increase the risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

 In contrast, protective measures like condom use and proper medical care reduce the risk.

questions.questionText: Two women were decided not to have pregnancy in the near future and they were offered two different contraceptive options. In woman I, the material fitted over uterus did not allow the sperm to fertilize the egg. In woman II, the contraceptive prevented hormone production and the releasing of eggs from the ovaries. Which type of contraceptive methods did woman I and II used, respectively?
options: Post pill and Copper-coated intrauterine device
Copper-coated intrauterine device and contraceptive injection
questions.explanation:
Woman I used a copper-coated intrauterine device (IUD), which is fitted in the uterus and prevents sperm from fertilizing the egg. 

Woman II used a contraceptive injection (like Depo-Provera), which suppresses hormone production, preventing ovulation and thus pregnancy.

questions.questionText: Which tissues of plant leaves are involved in waterproofing, major photosynthetic and major gas exchange activities, respectively?
options: Guard cells, palisade mesophyll and epidermis
Guard cells, palisade mesophyll and spongy mesophyll
Waxy cuticle, palisade mesophyll and spongy mesophyll
Waxy cuticle, palisade mesophyll and epidermis
questions.explanation:
In plant leaves: 

- The waxy cuticle provides waterproofing to prevent water loss.

- The palisade mesophyll contains chloroplasts and is the major site of photosynthesis.

- The spongy mesophyll has air spaces facilitating major gas exchange (CO₂ and O₂) within the leaf.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the movement of water in plants? It moves
options: across the phloem tissue by diffusion.
across the tissues of a plant by osmosis.
by using energy until it reaches to the xylem.
questions.explanation: Water moves in plants mainly by **osmosis**, from regions of higher water potential (soil) to lower water potential (root cells and other tissues). It moves passively without using energy, primarily through the cell membranes and tissues until it reaches the xylem for upward transport.

questions.questionText: What will happen to the growth of the plant when you remove indole-acetic acid from the main shoot part of the plant?
options: The main shoot of the plant elongates.
The growth of side shoots will slow down.
questions.explanation:
Indole-acetic acid (IAA) is an auxin that promotes apical dominance, suppressing the growth of lateral (side) shoots.

 If IAA is removed from the main shoot, apical dominance is lost, allowing the side shoots to grow more rapidly, causing the plant to become bushy.

questions.questionText: Select the option that the whole lists contain renewable natural resources.
options: Coal, oil, natural gas and minerals
Coal, wind, hydro power and biomass
Sunlight, wind, hydro power and biomass
Sunlight, wind, hydro power and natural gas
questions.explanation:
Renewable natural resources are those that can be replenished naturally in a short period. 

Sunlight, wind, hydro power, and biomass** are all renewable, whereas coal, oil, natural gas, and minerals are non-renewable resources.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following list of activities.
I. Establishing national parks
II. Wild sanctuaries
III. Preparing wild life reserves
IV. Practicing overgrazing
Which of the above activities CANNOT be used for the conservation of wild life?
questions.explanation:
Practicing overgrazing is harmful to the environment and destroys wildlife habitats, so it cannot be used for wildlife conservation.

 Activities I (national parks), II (wild sanctuaries), and III (wildlife reserves) are all strategies for conserving wildlife.

questions.questionText: The structural basis of water's high surface tension lies in its:
questions.explanation: Surface tension is a direct result of the strong cohesive forces (hydrogen bonds) pulling the water molecules at the surface together.

questions.questionText: Robert Koch is famous for formulating a set of criteria used to determine:
options: The structure of the DNA molecule
The microbial cause of a specific disease
questions.explanation: Robert Koch established the microbial cause of specific diseases using what is now known as Koch's postulates.

questions.questionText: The final product of meiosis is typically:
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two cell divisions, resulting in four genetically distinct, haploid cells (gametes).

questions.questionText: What will happen if an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant? The:
questions.explanation:
Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation and cell division.

When an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant, the hormone stimulates stem growth, making the plant taller.

The other options (leaf fall, side shoot growth, root storage) are not primary effects of gibberellins.

questions.questionText: Which inorganic ion is vital for both nerve function and muscle contraction?
questions.explanation: Calcium ions trigger the release of neurotransmitters in nerves and initiate the sliding of filaments in muscle contraction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes increases the genetic variation in gametes?
questions.explanation: These two events, unique to Meiosis I, scramble the parental genes, creating new allele combinations.

questions.questionText: The alignment of all chromosomes along the middle plane of the cell is the hallmark of which mitotic phase?
questions.explanation: Metaphase is defined by the arrangement of chromosomes on the metaphase plate (the imaginary plane equidistant from the two poles).

questions.questionText: Pulmonary circulation differs from systemic circulation in that it is a circulation that
options: pumps blood to the wall of lungs via coronary artery.
carries deoxygenated blood via pulmonary vein.
takes place between the heart and the lungs.
supplies oxygenated blood to the rest body parts.
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circulation is the pathway of blood flow specifically between the heart and the lungs, whereas systemic circulation transports blood between the heart and the rest of the body.

questions.questionText: In humans (2n = 46), how many chromosomes are present in a cell at the beginning of Meiosis II?
questions.explanation: Meiosis I reduces the chromosome number to the haploid number (23). Each chromosome still has two chromatids.

questions.questionText: What holds the sister chromatids together at the center before they separate in anaphase?
questions.explanation: The centromere is the region of the chromosome that holds the two sister chromatids together until anaphase.

questions.questionText: What is the key difference that distinguishes a saturated fatty acid from an unsaturated fatty acid?
options: Saturated fats are liquid at room temperature.
Saturated fats have at least one Carbon=Carbon double bond.
Saturated fats have only single Carbon-Carbon bonds (are saturated with hydrogen).
Unsaturated fats are used for insulation.
questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids lack Carbon=Carbon double bonds, making their chains straight and allowing them to pack tightly, typically resulting in a solid fat at room temperature.

questions.questionText: Why is water considered the universal solvent in biology?
options: Because it is odorless and tasteless.
Because it is a gas at high temperatures.
Because its polarity allows it to dissolve a wide range of ionic and polar substances.
Because it is the only molecule that can form hydrogen bonds.
questions.explanation: Water's polarity allows its partially charged ends to interact with and separate other charged molecules, effectively dissolving them.

questions.questionText: The phloem tissue, an essential component of the vascular bundle, is primarily responsible for the translocation of:
options: Synthesized food (sugars) to all parts of the plant
questions.explanation: Phloem transports synthesized food (sugars, which are the products of photosynthesis) to the different tissues of the plant, including the roots and growing points.

questions.questionText: The development of a new bio-fuel from algae is an example of the successful outcome of which field?
questions.explanation: Developing new products or technologies like bio-fuel is a characteristic of applied biology or biotechnology, which uses fundamental biological knowledge for practical application.

questions.questionText: The duct that carries urine from the kidney down to the urinary bladder is the:
questions.explanation: The ureter transports urine via peristalsis to the bladder for storage.

questions.questionText: What is the primary event that occurs during the Synthesis (S) phase of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: The S phase is when the cell synthesizes a complete copy of its DNA, resulting in duplicated chromosomes (sister chromatids).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following monohybrid crosses can be a test cross?
questions.explanation:
A test cross is always performed by crossing an organism with an unknown genotype (usually dominant phenotype) with an organism that is homozygous recessive (rr).

 This allows a scientist to determine the genotype of the first organism.
 Among the options, RR x rr (crossing a homozygous dominant with a homozygous recessive) is a type of cross used in Mendelian genetics and fits the definition of crossing with the recessive parent (though Rr x rr is the most common test cross).

questions.questionText: The main component of the shoot system that is responsible for connecting the root to the leaves and supporting the plant's upright growth is the:
questions.explanation: The stem is a primary axis of the plant that gives support, keeps the plant erect, and connects the root system to the leaves and flowers.

questions.questionText: In the process of photosynthesis, water acts primarily as a source of:
questions.explanation: During the light-dependent reactions, water is split (photolysis) to provide the necessary electrons and Hydrogen ions (protons) for the synthesis of ATP and NADPH.

questions.questionText: Which phase of mitosis is essentially the reverse of prophase, involving the reformation of the nuclear envelope?
questions.explanation: In telophase, the nuclear envelope and nucleoli reform, and chromosomes decondense back into chromatin.

questions.questionText: Which two sciences are essential to understanding the movement of water from the root to the leaves of a plant due to cohesion and capillary action?
questions.explanation: Water conduction involves Physics (cohesion/capillary action) and Chemistry (molecular structure of water).

questions.questionText: Walia ibex is an endemic animal species in Ethiopia which is found in
questions.explanation: The Walia Ibex (Capra walie) is an endemic and critically endangered wild goat species found almost exclusively in the Simien Mountains National Park in northern Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: The conversion of Glucose to Glycogen in the liver is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Building a large polymer (Glycogen) from monomers (Glucose) requires joining them by removing water, which is a Condensation reaction.

questions.questionText: The cambium, found between the xylem and phloem in a dicot vascular bundle, is composed of actively dividing young cells whose main function is to facilitate:
questions.explanation: The cambium is a strip of actively dividing cells (meristematic tissue) that produces secondary xylem and phloem, resulting in an increase in the stem's girth (secondary growth/widening).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following plant species is endemic to Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: In the chemical formula (CH2O)n, n=6 represents which class of carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: When n=6, the formula is C6H12O6, which corresponds to the hexose **monosaccharides** like glucose and fructose.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the process of digestion in humans? It involves
options: breaks down of large food molecules into absorbable end products.
mechanical breakdown of carbohydrates into maltose in the small intestine.
enzyme and secretions that best works at common optimum pH.
mechanical breakdown of larger molecules in the duodenum.
questions.explanation: Digestion is defined as the physical and chemical breakdown of large, insoluble food molecules into smaller, soluble end products that can be absorbed by the body.

questions.questionText: A cell that possesses two sets of chromosomes (one from each parent) is described as:
questions.explanation: Diploid cells have two homologous copies of each chromosome, characteristic of somatic cells.

questions.questionText: How do phospholipids arrange themselves in an aqueous environment to form a bilayer?
options: Hydrophobic tails facing the water, hydrophilic heads facing the interior.
Hydrophobic heads facing the water, hydrophilic tails facing the interior.
Hydrophilic heads facing the water, hydrophobic tails facing the interior.
They form a single layer with no organization.
questions.explanation: To minimize energy, the hydrophilic heads face the water (outside/inside the cell), while the hydrophobic tails cluster away from the water in the middle.

questions.questionText: The breeding mechanism that improves the performance of animals or plants using particular traits is
questions.explanation:
Selective breeding (also called artificial selection) is the process by which humans choose organisms with desirable characteristics and intentionally breed them together over generations. 

The goal is to enhance specific, useful traits (like high yield in crops or fast running speed in animals) to improve the performance of animals or plants.

questions.questionText: In the human body, the role of Cl- ions is critical for the production of acid in which organ?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions (Cl-) are used by parietal cells in the **stomach** lining to form Hydrochloric Acid (HCl).

questions.questionText: Which type of protein is responsible for fighting infections by recognizing and neutralizing foreign bodies?
questions.explanation: Antibodies, or Immunoglobulins, are highly specific defense proteins that bind to antigens on pathogens.

questions.questionText: A patient exhibited symptoms of weight loss, sweating, and irritability and the doctor suspected an endocrine malfunction that can be related to the
questions.explanation: Unexplained weight loss, excessive sweating (heat intolerance), and irritability are classic symptoms of hyperthyroidism, an overproduction of hormones by the thyroid gland.

questions.questionText: During which phase of the cell cycle does the cell grow and synthesize proteins, but NOT yet replicate its DNA?
questions.explanation: The G1 phase is the first gap phase where the cell grows and prepares for the S phase, but DNA synthesis has not begun.

questions.questionText: Short sightedness is corrected by a concave lens because the problem arises due to a
options: weak eye lens that converges light slightly.
powerful eye lens that diverges light.
weak eye lens that diverges light.
strong eye lens that converges light too soon.
questions.explanation:
Short sightedness (myopia) occurs when the lens is too strong (or the eyeball is too long), causing light to be focused in front of the retina.

 A concave (diverging) lens is needed to push the focal point back.

questions.questionText: The organelle in plant cells that is the site of photosynthesis and contains the pigment chlorophyll is the:
questions.explanation: The chloroplast is the photosynthetic apparatus in plant cells, and it contains chlorophyll, the green pigment necessary to capture light energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about mitosis? It:
options: produces four different daughter cells from a single cell.
is the division of sex cells resulting in identical daughter cells.
produces half number of chromosomes from the original cell.
is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the process by which somatic (body) cells divide to produce two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell and contain the full (diploid) chromosome number.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a universal characteristic of all organisms belonging to the Kingdom Plantae?
questions.explanation: Plants are defined as autotrophic organisms (producers) that use sunlight to make their own food through photosynthesis. Vascular tissue and flowers are only characteristics of higher plants.

questions.questionText: Which part of the stem, found in the vascular bundle of dicots, is responsible for the radial expansion of the stem?
questions.explanation: The cambium is the meristematic layer that divides to form secondary xylem and phloem, resulting in the thickening (radial expansion) of the stem.

questions.questionText: If a plant is grown in total darkness, which essential process related to its survival will cease, causing it to eventually perish?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires light (sunlight) and ceases in darkness. Without food production, the plant cannot sustain itself and will die. Respiration, transpiration, and absorption continue for a time.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a common and universal practice regarding blood transfusion?
options: Blood group compatibility has to be confirmed before transfusion.
The genetic background of the donor must be checked against the recipients.
The donors must be a close relative of the recipient to avoid any potential serious reactions.
Analyzing the donor's family background and nutritional status so far.
questions.explanation: Matching and testing blood group compatibility (ABO and Rh factor) prior to transfusion is required globally to prevent life-threatening immune agglutination and hemolysis.

questions.questionText: A cell that loses control over its cell cycle and begins to divide uncontrollably may develop into what disease?
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled cell division due to failures in cell cycle regulation is the fundamental cause of cancer.

questions.questionText: What is the key difference in cytokinesis between plant and animal cells?
options: Animals use spindle fibers; plants use microtubules.
Plants form a cell plate; animals form a cleavage furrow.
Animals use nuclear envelope reformation; plants use chromosome decondensation.
Plants use cytokinesis; animals do not.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall, so they build a cell plate to divide; animal cells are flexible and use a cleavage furrow.

questions.questionText: Which of the following shows a pair of 'pure' and its 'applied' sub-fields of biology?
questions.explanation: Botany is the pure theoretical science of plant biology, and plant breeding is an applied science derived from botany and genetics.

questions.questionText: This item is based on the following diagram of the human ear. What is the name of the human ear part represented by letter 'F' in the above diagram?
questions.explanation: The letter 'F' points to the coiled, snail-shell-like organ that contains the sensory receptors for hearing, which is the Cochlea.

questions.questionText: If a cell skips the G2 phase, what is the most likely consequence during M phase?
questions.explanation: The G2 phase is crucial for ensuring all DNA is replicated and undamaged. Skipping it could lead to errors in chromosome sorting.

questions.questionText: What is the term for the resulting cell when a sperm and an egg fuse during fertilization?
questions.explanation: The fusion of two haploid gametes forms a diploid zygote, which develops into a new organism.

questions.questionText: During which phase of mitosis do the chromosomes first become visible as distinct, condensed structures?
questions.explanation: Prophase is the first stage where chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

questions.questionText: What separates during Anaphase I of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Anaphase I separates the homologous chromosomes, moving the maternal and paternal chromosomes to opposite poles.

questions.questionText: Which monosaccharide is the primary source of energy for cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Glucose is the key sugar broken down during cellular respiration to produce ATP.

questions.questionText: In which phase of the cell cycle is a cell typically spending the most time?
questions.explanation: Interphase is the longest phase, where the cell conducts most of its growth, metabolism, and prepares for division.

questions.questionText: Which factor is LEAST likely to cause a protein to denature?
questions.explanation: Mild cooling will typically slow down an enzyme's activity but will not cause the irreversible unfolding (denaturation) of its structure.

questions.questionText: The separation of sister chromatids is the defining event of which mitotic phase?
questions.explanation: In anaphase, the cohesion proteins are cleaved, allowing the sister chromatids (now individual chromosomes) to separate and move to opposite poles.

questions.questionText: In the process of cytokinesis in animal cells, what structure is responsible for pinching the cell into two?
questions.explanation: The cleavage furrow, an indentation in the cell surface, is formed by a ring of actin filaments that contract to divide the cytoplasm.

questions.questionText: In the process of photosynthesis, the raw materials are carbon dioxide and water. Which of the following is the final primary product and an essential by-product, respectively?
questions.explanation: The overall equation for photosynthesis is 6CO2 + 6H2O --> Light, Chlorophyll  C6H12O6 + 6O2. Glucose is the food product, and Oxygen is the essential by-product.

questions.questionText: Which event is NOT a function of mitosis in multicellular organisms?
questions.explanation: Gamete production (sperm and egg) occurs through meiosis, not mitosis.

questions.questionText: The plant Justicia schimperiana (known as Besobilla) is used in Ethiopian traditional medicine to treat:
questions.explanation: The medicinal plant Besobilla (Justicia schimperiana) is used orally to treat abdominal pain.

questions.questionText: This item is based on the table below that compares meiosis and mitosis.
questions.explanation: Row 1 is correct (meiosis yields unique cells for sexual reproduction; mitosis yields identical cells). Row 3 is correct (both begin after DNA replication in interphase). Row 4 is correct (meiosis drives genetic variation essential for evolution; mitosis is used for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction). Row 2 is incorrect because it swaps the chromosome numbers (meiosis halves chromosome number while mitosis maintains it).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT about seed dispersal?
options: The mechanism of seed dispersal is related to the structural adaptations and overall nature of seeds.
Seed dispersal is necessary to avoid overcrowding and biological competitions between growing seedlings.
Water is the main seed dispersal agent for seeds that are covered with hard seed coats.
Different seed dispersal mechanisms ensure plant distribution across wide areas because plants are sessile.
questions.explanation: Having a hard seed coat is an adaptation primarily for protection or dormancy; water dispersal specifically requires adaptations like buoyant, spongy, or air-filled structures (e.g., coconuts) rather than just a hard coat.

questions.questionText: The mitotic spindle is composed of what type of cytoskeletal elements?
questions.explanation: The spindle fibers are made up of microtubules that attach to the chromosomes and pull them apart.

questions.questionText: A student placed a piece of bread in moist environment and after a few days he observed the growth of a fuzzy organism on the bread. How did the organism obtain nutrients required for its growth? By
options: synthesizing organic molecules using light energy
decomposing the nutrient extracellularly and absorbing it
hydrolyzing organic matter intracellularly and transporting it
directly ingesting the organic matter using phagocytosis
questions.explanation: Bread mold (fungi) exhibits saprotrophic nutrition, secreting digestive enzymes extracellularly to break down complex organic matter and then absorbing the soluble nutrients.

questions.questionText: In Metaphase I, what structures align along the metaphase plate?
questions.explanation: In Meiosis I, the paired homologous chromosomes align as bivalents at the center.

questions.questionText: Which field integrates the structure and function of informational molecules like DNA and RNA with cellular processes?
questions.explanation: Molecular Biology is the study of structure and function of informational molecules such as DNA and RNA.

questions.questionText: Mitosis produces daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell. What term describes this outcome?
questions.explanation: Because mitosis produces exact copies, the daughter cells are genetic clones of the parent cell.

questions.questionText: In the human digestive system, the pancreas is a gland that has two major functions: exocrine (digestive enzymes) and endocrine (hormones). (True or False)
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes digestive enzymes into the small intestine (exocrine) and insulin/glucagon into the blood (endocrine).

questions.questionText: Which of the following plant groups relies exclusively on spores for reproduction and lacks flowers and seeds?
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes (ferns) are vascular plants that reproduce via spores and do not produce seeds or flowers.

questions.questionText: What is the key source of genetic variation that occurs in Prophase I of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, creating new allele combinations.

questions.questionText: What is the primary storage polysaccharide found in animal liver and muscle cells?
questions.explanation: Glycogen is the compact, branched polymer used by animals to store excess glucose.

questions.questionText: If an organism's diploid number (2n) is 12, what is the haploid number (n) of its gametes after meiosis?
questions.explanation: The haploid number (n) is half the diploid number (2n); 12 / 2 = 6.

questions.questionText: The girdling experiment (ringing experiment), where a ring of outer bark is removed from a stem, demonstrates that the tissue responsible for transporting manufactured food is the:
options: Xylem, located in the inner wood
Phloem, located just beneath the bark
Pith, located at the center of the stem
questions.explanation: When the outer bark is removed, the phloem tissue is cut, but the xylem remains intact. The swelling observed above the cut proves that food transport (which is cut off) occurs in the phloem.

questions.questionText: The two-step bacterial process that converts ammonium (NH4+) to nitrite (NO2-) and then to nitrate (NO3-) is known as:
questions.explanation: Nitrification is a two-step process: Nitrosomonas bacteria convert ammonium to nitrite, and then Nitrobacter bacteria convert nitrite to the usable form, nitrate (NO3-).

questions.questionText: What structure is composed of duplicated DNA and associated proteins, visible during cell division?
questions.explanation: A chromosome is the organized structure of DNA and protein that is condensed during mitosis and meiosis.

questions.questionText: The term used to describe the total mass of living organisms at a specific trophic level is:
questions.explanation: Biomass is the total dry mass of organic matter present at a given time at a particular trophic level in an ecosystem. Standing crop is the amount of biomass at a specific time.

questions.questionText: The force of Transpiration Pull is effective in moving water column upwards due to the properties of water, such as cohesion and adhesion. This phenomenon is a biological example of the application of:
questions.explanation: Cohesion and adhesion are physical properties of water molecules that contribute to surface tension and capillary action, concepts rooted in Physics.

questions.questionText: Meiosis I is referred to as the reduction division because it reduces the number of:
options: Homologous pairs from four to two.
Daughter cells from four to two.
questions.explanation: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes, reducing the ploidy level from diploid (2n) to haploid (n).

questions.questionText: The paired homologous chromosomes in Prophase I are referred to as a:
questions.explanation: A bivalent or tetrad consists of one homologous pair, comprising four sister chromatids.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following diagram of parts of a flower.

In the above diagram, which part of a flower is represented by letter A?
questions.explanation: Letter A points to the growing pollen tube descending through the style towards the ovule.

questions.questionText: The process where necessary substances like glucose, amino acids, and water are selectively moved back from the renal tubules into the blood is called:
questions.explanation: Tubular reabsorption is a vital process to retain valuable molecules and water, preventing them from being lost in the urine.

questions.questionText: The condition where a person has an extra copy of chromosome 21 (Trisomy 21) results in which disorder?
questions.explanation: Down Syndrome is the most common condition resulting from nondisjunction of an autosome.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT the function of the liver?
questions.explanation:
The liver functions include storing glycogen, controlling cholesterol levels, and forming bile.

 However, monosaccharide metabolism primarily occurs in the cells of the body (e.g., glycolysis in cytoplasm) rather than being a direct function of the liver.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main function of Bowman's capsule of the human kidneys?
questions.explanation: Bowman's capsule surrounds the glomerulus and performs ultrafiltration, filtering blood plasma (including water, ions, and small molecules) into the nephron while retaining blood cells and large proteins in the blood.

questions.questionText: What tissue connects bone to bone at a joint?
questions.explanation: Ligaments stabilize joints and prevent excessive movement.

questions.questionText: The overall purpose of Photosynthesis for the plant is the conversion of light energy into which form of stored energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process that converts radiant light energy into chemical energy stored in organic molecules like glucose.

questions.questionText: Why are lichens considered pioneer species in primary succession?
options: They are large trees that provide shade.
They can grow on bare rock and initiate soil formation.
They require pre-existing soil to thrive.
questions.explanation:
Lichens are capable of growing on surfaces like bare rock where no soil exists. 
They physically and chemically break down the rock, creating the initial organic matter needed for soil, thus pioneering primary succession.

questions.questionText: Meiosis II is essentially identical to which other process?
questions.explanation: Meiosis II is an equational division like mitosis, where sister chromatids separate.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following shows a correct match between the component and function of the human lymphatic system?
options: Lymph nodes - produces and transport red blood cells
Lymphatic vessels - transport fluid to the body tissues
Lymphatic trunk - collects and fight pathogens
questions.explanation: Lymph is a fluid that circulates throughout the lymphatic system, carrying white blood cells (lymphocytes) to help fight infection.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key characteristic of non-flowering plants (Gymnosperms) like the pine tree?
options: Seed formation occurs in a fruit.
They have naked seeds borne in cones.
Their life cycle lacks a dominant sporophyte stage.
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are non-flowering seed plants, and their characteristic feature is that their seeds are 'naked' (not enclosed) and typically produced in cones.
